findings.title: GitHub user check is skipped when no Integration row exists yet
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist (around line 481-482), the view returns pipeline.next_step() immediately. The new check that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user matches the installing sender (around lines 501-505) only runs when the Integration row already exists. If the installation webhook has not arrived yet, or the row is absent for any other reason, a user can complete the pipeline with an arbitrary installation_id without ever being checked against the installer. That defeats the purpose of this PR, and the check should also run on that path, or the path should be made to fail.

findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata has no sender
findings.body: The comparison uses integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. build_integration only stores "sender" in metadata when state.get("sender") is truthy, so an integration without a stored sender raises KeyError and the request returns a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use a safe lookup and fail closed, e.g. treat a missing sender as a mismatch.

findings.title: Network failures during OAuth exchange are not handled
findings.body: The call req = safe_urlopen(...) on the access-token exchange sits outside the try block. Likewise get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) is not guarded. A connection error or timeout to GitHub raises an unhandled exception and produces a 500 rather than the install-failed page, and the user cannot recover without restarting the flow.

findings.title: State and redirect_uri are interpolated into the authorize URL without encoding
findings.body: The OAuth authorize URL is built with f-string interpolation of state and redirect_uri without urlencode. The redirect_uri contains a scheme and slashes, which can break or alter query parsing on the GitHub side. Build the query with urlencode to be safe.

findings.title: 404 installation-not-found path no longer tested
findings.body: test_installation_not_found previously asserted the specific 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' message. The changed test now only sends a second request with a different state and asserts the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message. The original 404 behavior is no longer covered, and the new assertion can be satisfied by an unrelated failure.

findings.title: Brittle responses.calls index in assert_setup_flow
findings.body: The assertion reads responses.calls[2] to find the JWT Authorization header. The index now depends on how many OAuth and user calls happen before it, so unrelated stub changes will break it or make it check the wrong request. Locate the call by URL instead.
